registered_in: docs/evolution/w3/stab2/F14-V4-PROTOCOL.md (F14 v4, approved by the owner on 2026-11-09)
hypothesis: Memory promoted by the owner, delivered by the production agent run with source_db, makes the model apply a real project convention to inputs the note does not list, as judged by protected tests on the final file.

conditions.control: box A (criterion): the own note, written as agent memory (untrusted), NOT promoted
conditions.promoted: box B (criterion): the own note, promoted by the owner in the owner terminal
conditions.placebo: box C (informative, no inference): the note of ANOTHER task (oidc gets seed, seed gets pass, pass gets oidc), promoted by the owner; the own note does not exist in this box; memory id f14v4-<task>-placebo

pilots.rule: a pilot that passes the protected tests rejects the task; the series then cannot run

promotion.distribution: 3 in box B (own notes) + 3 in box C (placebo notes)
promotion.command: hseos memory promote --db <banco> --project <projeto> --memory <id> --reason "<motivo>" --operator owner (needs a TTY, one memory at a time)
promotion.rule: the campaign script NEVER promotes in real mode: `prepare` prints the 6 commands, the owner runs them, and `verify-promotions` (also run before the first call) checks trust, content sha256 and operator; any divergence is BLOCKED

seed.drawn: at campaign start, from the OS entropy source

order: per task a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle of 5 control + 5 promoted + 3 placebo runs; task order also shuffled; pilots first

analysis.test: exact conditional stratified (convolution of hypergeometrics), promoted against control, two-sided, p = sum of probabilities <= observed
analysis.success: in EVERY task promoted >= 4/5 and control <= 1/5, AND p < 0.05
analysis.placebo: descriptive only: successes per task out of 3, no inference
analysis.informative: requests per run and per arm, how many runs hit the request cap, note_in_context (own note in the context) and memory sources per run
analysis.primary_outcome: protected tests pass on the final file rebuilt from the ledger AND the product verifier approves; no reconstruction is no-final-write with a reason, never an approval; hitting the cap is a separate datum, not the outcome

budget.ceiling_scope: cumulative over the whole campaign, by the spend ESTIMATED by the script WITH the published cache discount (the no-cache cost is recorded beside it): prior_spend_usd + spend of the campaign + worst-case projection of the next call never exceeds ceiling_usd
budget.prior_spend_note: v4 is a new campaign: nothing was spent before it. The 80% stop rule does not apply
budget.credit_precondition: the credit of the account must be at least US$ 3.00 at the start (read from the console by the owner before launch); otherwise the campaign does not start
budget.effective_ceiling_rule: in real mode the effective ceiling is min(ceiling_usd, credit_usd - credit_reserve_usd), the credit being the one read from the console and declared with --credit-usd
budget.price_rule: real mode needs --price-in and --price-out explicitly (finite, > 0) and equal to this registered price; otherwise it aborts before the first call. There is no built-in price for real mode
budget.price_note: operator-declared USD per million tokens; cached input charged at the input price times cached_input_fraction (declared discount, not verified); an estimate, not an invoice
budget.max_requests_note: declared before any data (the v3 limit of 8 punished the control by exhaustion). A run that needs more is stopped by the guard: the ORIGINAL adapter proof is kept untouched, the run is marked cap_reached and counted apart
budget.per_request_check: before each call: prior_spend_usd + spent + worst-case projection (body bytes / 3 as tokens + max_tokens at the output price) > ceiling refuses the call
budget.unreadable_usage: the first request with unreadable usage ends the run as usage-unreadable and the campaign stops; the call is charged at the worst-case projection
budget.interrupted_request: a request cut by the 280 s timeout is charged with the declared context window as input plus max_tokens as output and is written to the request log

cap_reached_rule.proof: never rewritten: requests_total and backend_verified stay as the adapter reported them
cap_reached_rule.counting: a cap_reached run does not count as "adapter proof pass"; the receipt reports how many there were
cap_reached_rule.stop: it does NOT stop the campaign as a protocol failure, but only when the checks that do not depend on the count pass (observed model = declared, observed origin = declared, no pool, no fallback, credential source request-header); if any fails, it is a protocol failure and the campaign stops
cap_reached_rule.any_other_proof_not_pass: a run that did not hit the cap and whose proof is not pass stops the campaign

confirmation.rule: real mode runs only when the variable equals the hash printed by `f14v4.cjs --print-confirmation`; otherwise BLOCKED before any call
confirmation.covers: this plan, the prices, the protected cases and the content of the scripts listed in confirmation.cjs (GATED_FILES), including the v3 files the campaign imports; not the rehearsal results

stop: failed series ends the campaign with no extra round; the cumulative ceiling is a hard stop (STOPPED: cumulative ceiling)

limits_declared.real_path_never_exercised: The real path (network, the key, `hseos memory promote` in a TTY) was never exercised by this script: no real call, no real key and no TTY promotion took place while it was written or tested.
limits_declared.rehearsal_scope: The rehearsal uses a programmed fake model and only proves the plumbing (boxes, retrieval, meter, receipts, stop rules); it says nothing about what the real model does.
limits_declared.credit_declared_not_verified: The credit (--credit-usd) is declared by the operator from the console; the script does not verify it.
limits_declared.cost_is_estimate: The cost against the US$ 3.00 ceiling is the script estimate from the declared price with the published cached-input discount (cached_input_fraction 0.5, declared, not verified) applied to the cached_tokens the provider reports; it is not an invoice and the console prevails. In the previous execution the no-cache basis overstated the cost by 100% (US$ 2.98 estimated against US$ 1.49 charged by the console); the estimate with a 50% discount would have given US$ 1.94 on the same usage, still above the console; the real discount observed was between 50% and 75%; the console reading can lag.
failure_paths_covered: response that is not an event stream (usage unreadable)
request cut by the timeout (stops at the first occurrence)
request cap reached (original proof kept, counted apart)
observed model or origin diverging from the declared one
count-independent proof checks failing on a capped run
promotions missing, edited manifest, wrong sha256, wrong operator, control box altered or promoted
missing or wrong confirmation, price, credit, key, relative root, heavy-run ancestor or unreadable process ancestry
failure_paths_not_covered: real provider HTTP errors (4xx, 5xx, 429 rate limit) and network or DNS failure
a stream truncated in the middle of an event
key revoked or credit exhausted in the middle of the campaign
the provider changing the model behind the same dated name
the campaign process killed (SIGKILL) in the middle of a run, and any resume
the interactive `hseos memory promote` flow itself (TTY, confirmation prompt)
divergence between the script estimate and the console cost
limits_declared.product_files_static: PRODUCT_FILES is a static list derived from an execution trace in a fixture run, not recomputed. 9 files reachable by a static require from hseos-cli.js are not in it (governed-action, entrypoint-adapters, agent-environment/dap, dap-host, framing, browser-contract, legacy-mcp-server, mcp-transport, mcp-protocol), probably lazy requires outside the agent run path; this is not proved.
limits_declared.hash_fail_closed_files: package.json and tools/cli/command-manifest.json are in the hash, so changing either invalidates the confirmation (fail-closed).
limits_declared.hash_not_covered: The hash does not cover node_modules, the Node version or the content of the real project.db (only the sha256 of its copy is recorded).
limits_declared.heavy_run_detection: The heavy-run detection is a regex over the process command line and can wrongly BLOCK a legitimate run (BLOCKED with no cost).
limits_declared.promoted_id_format: The format of the promoted_id written by `hseos memory promote` in a real TTY was not exercised; verify-promotions expects `<memory_id>:promoted` as the product store produces it in the API path.
limits_declared.credit_lock_scope: The credit lock (effective ceiling = min(3.00, credit - 0.10)) only lowers the ceiling from 3.00 to 2.90 while the entry gate requires a credit >= 3.00; it does not protect a smaller credit. Changing that gate is an owner decision.
limits_declared.estimate_margin_over_console: The margin of the estimate with a 50% discount over the console was 0.4% in v3 (0.946 against 0.95) and 30% in v4 (1.94 against 1.49); the console prevails and the estimate is only safe if the real discount is at least 50%.
limits_declared.cached_tokens_invalid: An invalid cached_tokens (negative, string, NaN, null or absent) becomes 0 cached tokens (no discount, conservative); a value above prompt_tokens is clamped to prompt_tokens.
limits_declared.timeout_policy: A request cut by the timeout is charged at the pessimistic cost, written to the log and STOPS the campaign at the first occurrence (STOPPED: timeout). This differs from v3, which left the decision to the owner.

credential: read from F14V4_OPENAI_API_KEY, provided by the operator at execution time; never from pass; never written or printed
